messages:
Nora (People Ops): Quick heads-up  we have one request for a 'nomad pilot' where an engineer wants to spend 7 days in a different US state each month (rotating). Need guidance on WFH stipend, payroll withholding, and whether we allow recurring multi-state patterns.

Diego (Eng): Yep that was me. Plan is 7 days in a different city monthly to pair with regional partners. Want to keep stipend and avoid paperwork if possible.

Lina (Payroll): Short answer: recurring multi-state presence increases payroll complexity. If you remain <90 consecutive days in any single state, homebase stays the same for benefits, but we may still need to track state income source days for withholding/reporting.

Omar (Legal): Also note: even short, frequent trips can create nexus if you perform recruiting or sign contracts while there. Purely internal pairing is lower risk, but still recommend disclosing exact activities.

Sam (Finance): For stipend: we can either pro-rate based on days in homebase vs away, or keep full stipend and require pre-approval with manager+finance to accept the extra tax/admin burden. If you want full stipend across rotating states that's an exception request.

Diego (Eng): How would proration work when "away" is split across multiple states in the same month? Example: 7 days in CO, 7 in WA, 16 at home.

Lina (Payroll): We'll count total homebase days vs total days. Prorate by calendar days at homebase. So payout = (homebase_days/total_days_in_month) * stipend. We'll also record nonresident days per state for reporting.

Nora (People Ops): Process: 1) open People Ops case with the monthly rotation schedule and addresses; 2) include any client-facing or hiring activities; 3) confirm if coworking fees will be reimbursed or billed to Redwood. We'll respond with payroll/withholding notes and timeline.

PeopleOps-Bot: Case created #42781 "Diego - nomad pilot (7d/month different states)". Nora will triage.

Omar (Legal): If you plan to interview/hire occasionally while traveling, escalate before travel. That activity can change the analysis and may require approvals.

Sam (Finance): Practical note: submit cases at least 10 business days before payroll cutoff so we can calculate proration and any state withholding adjustments. Exceptions cause delays and retro taxes.

Diego (Eng): Cool. I'll open the case and list planned cities + activities. Thanks folks.

Nora (People Ops): We'll draft a short nomad pilot FAQ and an approval template for exceptions (full stipend requests). Posting draft in this thread when ready. :rocket:
